proof_summary: Lucas congruences modulo p pair the terms for indices k and p+k to show both sequences vanish at p+m for 0≤m≤p−2; at p−1, \(\binom{p-1}{k}\equiv(-1)^k\) gives the first boundary value 1, while divisibility of central binomial coefficients leaves only \(k=(p-1)/2\) in the second sum, giving \((-1)^{(p-1)/2}\). Thus each Hankel matrix is anti-triangular modulo p; reversing its columns makes it triangular with constant diagonal, and the reversal sign together with \(x^p=x\) modulo p yields the two determinant congruences.
